text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed sustained queue depth on the us-west-gpu shared pool since ~02:10 UTC. Tail latency up 3x and a few token charge spikes. Putting initial findings here.
oliver: seen it too. Any obvious tenant culprits? logs show a cluster of long-ctx requests but also lots of concurrent small first-token costs.
sophie: Data pipeline from tenant 'dataforge' had a retry storm (500s on their side) and kept reissuing embedding jobs. They also increased batch_size via the SDK without pinning model/version.
maya: exact — here's the jq filter I used on the request log:

```
cat requests.log | jq -r 'select(.region=="us-west1" and .gpu_pool=="shared") | {ts:.t, tenant:.tenant, tokens:.tokens, latency:.lat_ms} | @json'
```

maya: output shows many same-tenant bursts: 60k tokens over 10 min from ~15 concurrent connections.
akshay: oof. That will spike prefix cache pressure + KV thrash. Did autoscaler spin up more nodes or did queueing just block?
oliver: autoscaler attempted 2 scale-ups but saw allocation fragmentation (instances too small for 80-token contended workloads). New VMs saturated local NIC throughput and didn't help latency.
sophie: seems multi-factor: tenant retrying + fragmentation + network egress throttles in us-west1 evening window.
maya: short-term ops idea: apply a soft backpressure on that tenant with a small hold window (5m) and reduce their max concurrent in-flight to 6, keep other tenants unaffected. We can do via route policy override.
akshay: +1. Also suggest enabling token-bucket weighting: give other tenants an extra burst buffer to avoid cascade.
oliver: for the route override, use:

```
redwoodctl route update --pool shared-us-west --tenant dataforge --concurrency 6 --hold-window 300s --reason "retry-storm backpressure"
```

maya: I'll run the command if we agree. Who wants to own the revert/monitoring? I'll monitor queue depth & tail-p90.
sophie: I'll add a temporary alert rule: if shared-pool tail_p95 > 600ms for >2m then page infra oncall and post here. Also add a per-tenant ingress drop rate metric.
akshay: post-mortem/next steps: ask product to gate SDK batch_size change with tenant quoter or advisory; long-term: consider shard-aware allocation to avoid fragmenting bursts across NICs.
oliver: one more long-term idea: tenant signature detection — classify tenants by burstiness and move high-burst ones into a scheduled 'burst lane' with isolated eviction budget.
maya: agreed. For now I'm applying the route override.
ops-bot: deploy job queued: route-update-1977777777 by maya. Will report status.
ops-bot: route-update-1977777777 succeeded in 18s. concurrency set to 6, hold-window=300s.
maya: applied. Initial queue depth trending down within 90s. p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~420ms.
sophie: alert quiet. Looks stable for now. I'll keep the temp rule for 30m.
akshay: can we capture a sample of the offending requests and share to dataforge SRE? we should include request IDs and timestamps.
maya: grabbing samples and will DM SREs. Also proposing a short RFC for 'burst lane' and shard-aware packing next week.
oliver: nice triage everyone. If this recurs after 30m we'll escalate to capacity planning and consider a short, automated tenant penalty box.
sophie: filing a follow-up ticket: INFRA-6739 "Burst lane proposal + SDK batch gating" and linking this thread.
maya: closing loop — will update ticket and ping here when Dataforge confirms fixes. :thumbsup:
